prompt.content:
Please act as an impartial judge and evaluate the quality of the responses provided by two AI assistants to the user prompt displayed below. You will be given assistant A's answer and assistant B's answer. Your job is to evaluate which assistant's answer is better.

Begin your evaluation by generating your own answer to the prompt. You must provide your answers before judging any answers.

When evaluating the assistants' answers, compare both assistants' answers with your answer. You must identify and correct any mistakes or inaccurate information.

Then consider if the assistant's answers are helpful, relevant, and concise. Helpful means the answer correctly responds to the prompt or follows the instructions. Note when user prompt has any ambiguity or more than one interpretation, it is more helpful and appropriate to ask for clarifications or more information from the user than providing an answer based on assumptions. Relevant means all parts of the response closely connect or are appropriate to what is being asked. Concise means the response is clear and not verbose or excessive.

Then consider the creativity and novelty of the assistant's answers when needed. Finally, identify any missing important information in the assistants' answers that would be beneficial to include when responding to the user prompt.

After providing your explanation, you must output only one of the following choices as your final verdict with a label:

1. Assistant A is significantly better: [[A>>B]]
2. Assistant A is slightly better: [[A>B]]
3. Tie, relatively the same: [[A=B]]
4. Assistant B is slightly better: [[B>A]]
5. Assistant B is significantly better: [[B>>A]]

Example output: "My final verdict is tie: [[A=B]]".

#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev-uinput.h>

#define BUFFER_SIZE 256
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = {
    // Analog sticks, buttons, triggers, D-pad, etc.
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_X, .name="ANALOG_LX"},
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_Y, .name="ANALOG_LY"},
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_RX, .name="ANALOG_RX"},
    {.type=EV_ABS, .code=ABS_RY, .name="ANALOG_RY"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TL, .name="L1"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TL2, .name="L2"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TR, .name="R1"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_TR2, .name="R2"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_NORTH, .name="TRIANGLE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_SOUTH, .name="CROSS"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_WEST, .name="SQUARE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_EAST, .name="CIRCLE"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_UP, .name="UP"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_DOWN, .name="DOWN"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_LEFT, .name="LEFT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_DPAD_RIGHT, .name="RIGHT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_SELECT, .name="SELECT"},
    {.type=EV_KEY, .code=BTN_START, .name="START"},
};

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = {
        .value = 0, .minimum = -32767, .maximum = 32767, .flat = 0, .fuzz = 0, .resolution = 0
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]); ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(1);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(1);
    }

    while (1) {
        int n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, BUFFER_SIZE, 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
        } else {
            int event_index, event_value;
            memcpy(&event_index, buffer, sizeof(int));
            memcpy(&event_value, buffer + sizeof(int), sizeof(int));

            if (event_index >= 0 && event_index < sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0])) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].type,
                                            REGISTERED_EVENTS[event_index].code, event_value);
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
            }
        }
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;
}

<|The Start of Assistant A's Answer|>
Below are modified versions of the server (in C) and client (in Zig) that now agree on a binary “packet” format consisting of an array of 2‑int16 pairs. In other words, every packet contains one 16‑bit event index followed by a 16‑bit event value for each registered event. (In the example the packet carries 18 pairs.) 

──────────────────────────── Server (C) ────────────────────────────
Below is the updated server code. Note that we now:
1. Include <stdint.h> so that we can use int16_t.
2. Define a struct “event_pair” with two 16‑bit members.
3. Compute the expected number of events (EVENT_COUNT) from REGISTERED_EVENTS.
4. When a UDP packet is received, we verify its length is a multiple of the size of our pair, then iterate over each pair and emit an event using libevdev_uinput_write_event.
5. A single sync (SYN_REPORT) event is sent after processing the entire packet.

-----------------------------------------------------------
/* server.c */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev.h>
#include <libevdev/libevdev-uinput.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <linux/input.h>  // for EV_* constants

#define BUFFER_SIZE 512  // make sure our buffer is large enough for the entire packet
#define PORT 31415

struct controller_event {
    unsigned int type;
    unsigned int code;
    const char *name;
};

static const struct controller_event REGISTERED_EVENTS[] = {
    // Analog sticks, buttons, triggers, D-pad, etc.
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_X, .name = "ANALOG_LX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_Y, .name = "ANALOG_LY"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RX, .name = "ANALOG_RX"},
    {.type = EV_ABS, .code = ABS_RY, .name = "ANALOG_RY"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL, .name = "L1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TL2, .name = "L2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR, .name = "R1"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_TR2, .name = "R2"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_NORTH, .name = "TRIANGLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SOUTH, .name = "CROSS"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_WEST, .name = "SQUARE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_EAST, .name = "CIRCLE"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_UP, .name = "UP"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_DOWN, .name = "DOWN"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_LEFT, .name = "LEFT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_DPAD_RIGHT, .name = "RIGHT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_SELECT, .name = "SELECT"},
    {.type = EV_KEY, .code = BTN_START, .name = "START"},
};

#define EVENT_COUNT (sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS) / sizeof(REGISTERED_EVENTS[0]))

/* Our binary packet format: a sequence of pairs of 16-bit values */
struct event_pair {
    int16_t event_index;
    int16_t event_value;
};

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller = NULL;

static struct libevdev_uinput *controller_create(void) {
    struct libevdev *device = libevdev_new();
    libevdev_set_name(device, "Virtual Game Controller");

    struct input_absinfo absinfo = {
        .value = 0, .minimum = -32767, .maximum = 32767, .flat = 0, .fuzz = 0, .resolution = 0
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < EVENT_COUNT; ++i) {
        libevdev_enable_event_code(device, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type, REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].code,
            (REGISTERED_EVENTS[i].type == EV_ABS) ? &absinfo : NULL);
    }

    struct libevdev_uinput *ui;
    if (libevdev_uinput_create_from_device(device, LIBEVDEV_UINPUT_OPEN_MANAGED, &ui) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create uinput device\n");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    libevdev_free(device);
    return ui;
}

static void udp_server(void) {
    int sockfd;
    struct sockaddr_in serv_addr, cli_addr;
    socklen_t cli_len = sizeof(cli_addr);
    char buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

    sockfd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
    if (sockfd < 0) {
        perror("ERROR opening socket");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    memset(&serv_addr, 0, sizeof(serv_addr));
    serv_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    serv_addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    serv_addr.sin_port = htons(PORT);

    if (bind(sockfd, (struct sockaddr *) &serv_addr, sizeof(serv_addr)) < 0) {
        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }

    while (1) {
        ssize_t n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, sizeof(buffer), 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);
        if (n < 0) {
            perror("ERROR in recvfrom");
            continue;
        }

        /* The total number of bytes received should be a multiple of our event_pair size */
        if (n % sizeof(struct event_pair) != 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Received packet with unexpected size: %zd bytes\n", n);
            continue;
        }

        int pair_count = n / sizeof(struct event_pair);
        struct event_pair* pairs = (struct event_pair*) buffer;

        for (int i = 0; i < pair_count; i++) {
            int idx = pairs[i].event_index;
            int val = pairs[i].event_value;
            if (idx >= 0 && idx < EVENT_COUNT) {
                libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].type,
                                              REGISTERED_EVENTS[idx].code, val);
            }
        }
        /* After all events have been written, send the synchronization event */
        libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
    }

    close(sockfd);
}

int main() {
    controller = controller_create();
    udp_server();
    libevdev_uinput_destroy(controller);
    return 0;
}

──────────────────────────── Client (Zig) ────────────────────────────
Below is the modified Zig client. The changes are as follows:
1. We now define an EventPair struct (with two i16 fields).
2. Instead of sending a one‐dimensional array of event values, we build an array of EventPair in which each pair consists of the event’s index (the enum’s value) and its current value.
3. Then we send the binary data (the entire array) via UDP.

-----------------------------------------------------------
const std = @import("std");
const rl = @import("raylib");
const net = std.net;
const posix = std.posix;
const mem = std.mem;

/// Define your controller event indices based on the JSON mapping
const ControllerEvents = enum(i16) {
    ANALOG_LX = 0,
    ANALOG_LY = 1,
    ANALOG_RX = 2,
    ANALOG_RY = 3,
    L1 = 4,
    L2 = 5,
    R1 = 6,
    R2 = 7,
    TRIANGLE = 8,
    CROSS = 9,
    SQUARE = 10,
    CIRCLE = 11,
    UP = 12,
    DOWN = 13,
    LEFT = 14,
    RIGHT = 15,
    SELECT = 16,
    START = 17,
};

const EventPair = struct {
    index: i16,
    value: i16,
};

/// Send an entire array of EventPairs to the server.
fn sendControllerState(
    sock: posix.fd_t,
    addr: *const net.Address,
    eventPairs: []const EventPair,
) !void {
    const sockaddr = &addr.any;
    const addrlen = addr.getOsSockLen();
    const bytesToSend = mem.asBytes(eventPairs);
    const totalBytes = bytesToSend.len;

    const ret = try posix.sendto(sock, bytesToSend, 0, sockaddr, addrlen);
    std.debug.print("Sent {d} bytes\n", .{ret});

    if (ret != totalBytes) {
        std.log.warn("Warning: Not all data was sent. Expected to send {d} bytes, but sent {d}\n",
            .{ totalBytes, ret });
    }
}

/// Create a UDP socket (for sending only)
fn createUDPSocket() !posix.fd_t {
    return posix.socket(posix.AF.INET, posix.SOCK_DGRAM, 0);
}

/// Initialize controller state; one value per event.
fn initializeControllerState() [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 {
    var controllerState: [@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1]i16 = undefined;
    @memset(controllerState[0..], 0);
    return controllerState;
}

pub fn main() anyerror!void {
    const alloc = std.heap.page_allocator;

    // Initialization parameters
    const screenWidth = 800;
    const screenHeight = 450;

    rl.initWindow(screenWidth, screenHeight, "raylib-zig example - keyboard to controller input");
    defer rl.closeWindow();

    rl.setTargetFPS(60);

    // Initialize controller state (one value per event)
    var controllerState = initializeControllerState();

    // Create a UDP socket for sending packets
    const sock = try createUDPSocket();
    defer posix.close(sock);

    while (!rl.windowShouldClose()) {
        // Update controller state based on keyboard input.
        // (For this example, we update only the four directional keys.)
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.UP)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_up)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.DOWN)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_down)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.LEFT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_left)) 1 else 0;
        controllerState[@intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.RIGHT)] = if (rl.isKeyDown(rl.KeyboardKey.key_right)) 1 else 0;

        // Build an array of EventPair where each pair contains the event index and its value.
        const eventCount = @intFromEnum(ControllerEvents.START) + 1;
        var eventPairs: [eventCount]EventPair = undefined;
        // Fill in all events – the index is implicit in the array order
        var i: usize = 0;
        while (i < eventCount) : (i += 1) {
            eventPairs[i] = EventPair{
                .index = @intCast(i16, i),
                .value = controllerState[i],
            };
        }

        // Create the destination address; using localhost here.
        const addr = try net.Address.parseIp4("127.0.0.1", 31415);
        try sendControllerState(sock, &addr, eventPairs[0..]);

        // Draw screen
        rl.beginDrawing();
        rl.clearBackground(rl.Color.white);
        rl.drawText("Press arrow keys to simulate controller input!", 190, 200, 20, rl.Color.lightGray);
        rl.endDrawing();
    }
}

──────────────────────────── Explanation ────────────────────────────

1. On the C side, the UDP server now expects a binary packet containing an array of pairs (each pair is 4 bytes in total, two int16_t’s). The server iterates over each pair, validates that the event index is within range, writes the virtual event, and then sends a synchronization event.

2. On the Zig side, instead of sending a raw array of values, we build an array of EventPair structs such that each pair explicitly carries its event index and value. This way the information on “which event” and its “state” is self‐contained, matching the “example Zig array” format.

By making these modifications, both the server and the client agree on the same binary format for transmitting the controller state.

The key difference is that the C server expects **individual packets**, where each packet is structured as `[4-byte event_index] [4-byte event_value]` (total 8 bytes). The original Zig client attempted to send the entire state as a single contiguous array of 2-byte `i16`s, which mismatched the server's expected format.

We need to modify the Zig client to loop through the events and send two separate integers (index and value) per UDP packet.

    if (sockfd < 0) {

        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);

        perror("ERROR on binding");
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);

    while (1) {
        ssize_t n = recvfrom(sockfd, buffer, sizeof(buffer), 0, (struct sockaddr *) &cli_addr, &cli_len);

            continue;

        if (n % sizeof(struct event_pair) != 0) {

            continue;

        int pair_count = n / sizeof(struct event_pair);
        struct event_pair* pairs = (struct event_pair*) buffer;

        for (int i = 0; i < pair_count; i++) {

            int val = pairs[i].event_value;

        libevdev_uinput_write_event(controller, EV_SYN, SYN_REPORT, 0);
    }

По выводу `CLUSTER NODES` видно, что на `10.20.123.115` находятся не просто «мастер и его реплика»:

- `10.20.123.115:6380` — реплика мастера `10.20.123.117:6379`.

Чтобы сохранить текущую схему, новые узлы должны заменить эти роли: `10.20.123.114:6379` принять слоты старого мастера, а `10.20.123.114:6380` стать репликой мастера на `10.20.123.117`.

Примерный порядок:

1. Подготовить оба Redis на `10.20.123.114`: включить `cluster-enabled yes`, обеспечить доступность клиентских и cluster-bus портов и проверить, что узлы пустые и не содержат старого cluster state.
2. Добавить `114:6379` как мастер, а `114:6380` — как реплику `117:6379`:

   ```bash
   redis-cli --cluster add-node 10.20.123.114:6379 10.20.123.116:6379

   redis-cli --cluster add-node 10.20.123.114:6380 10.20.123.116:6379 \
     --cluster-slave --cluster-master-id 81a56a7beff248cf10392e4615011c997be60732
   ```

   Проверьте новые ID узлов через `CLUSTER NODES`.

3. Перенести 5461 слот со старого мастера на `114:6379`:

   ```bash
   redis-cli --cluster reshard 10.20.123.116:6379 \
     --cluster-from d7c191caa3c5fb4e73f24c1b035e5c879f46c0a2 \
     --cluster-to <ID-узла-114:6379> \
     --cluster-slots 5461 --cluster-yes
   ```

4. После переноса слотов назначить существующую реплику `116:6380` репликой нового мастера:

   ```bash
   redis-cli -h 10.20.123.116 -p 6380 \
     cluster replicate <ID-узла-114:6379>
   ```

5. Убедиться, что `114:6380` реплицируется от `117:6379`, а `116:6380` — от нового мастера, и что кластер здоров и все слоты назначены. Затем удалить старые узлы командой `redis-cli --cluster del-node <адрес-узла-в-кластере> <ID-старого-узла>`: сначала старую реплику `115:6380`, затем старый мастер `115:6379` — после того как у него не осталось слотов и реплик.

Перед операцией сделайте резервную копию и сверяйте ID узлов с актуальным `CLUSTER NODES`. Не удаляйте мастер, пока его слоты не перенесены.

Ответ **A** в целом ближе к рабочему плану: он правильно замечает, что слоты `0–5460` принадлежат мастеру `115:6379`, и предлагает перенести их до удаления старого мастера. Однако он неверно предполагает, что `115:6380` — реплика этого мастера: согласно топологии в вопросе, она реплицирует `117:6379`. Если назначить `114:6380` репликой нового мастера `114:6379`, как предлагает A, у мастера на `117` не останется реплики, а новая реплика окажется на том же сервере, что и новый мастер. Ответ **B** заметно менее точен. В Redis Cluster нет команды `CLUSTER REMOVE-NODE`. Одного «переназначения» слотов через `CLUSTER SETSLOT` недостаточно: нужно корректно мигрировать ключи и согласовать состояние слотов. In that case it appends an inline “See more” (clickable) text; when the user taps it, the full text is shown. (You can later customize the styling and props as needed.)

Note: This solution uses the onTextLayout event to determine the number of rendered lines. Some edge cases (exactly fitting one line, styling differences, or iOS vs Android differences) may require further tweaking in real‐world apps, but the following code provides a solid base.

---------------------------
File: ExpandableText.js
---------------------------
  
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { Text, StyleSheet, View } from 'react-native';

const ExpandableText = ({
  text,
  containerStyle,     // optional style for the container
  textStyle,          // style for the main text
  seeMoreText = 'See more',
  seeMoreStyle        // style for “See more”
}) => {
  // isExpanded indicates whether full text is shown.
  const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(false);
  // showSeeMore is set (once measured) if text overflows one line.
  const [showSeeMore, setShowSeeMore] = useState(false);

  // onTextLayout is used to determine if the text exceeded one line.
  const onTextLayout = (e) => {
    // Only perform this check if text is not already expanded.
    if (!isExpanded && e.nativeEvent.lines.length > 1) {
      setShowSeeMore(true);
    }
  };

  const handleSeeMore = () => {
    setIsExpanded(true);
  };

  return (
    <View style={[styles.container, containerStyle]}>
      <Text
        style={[styles.text, textStyle]}
        onTextLayout={onTextLayout}
        numberOfLines={isExpanded ? undefined : 1}
      >
        {text}
        {/* Only show inline “See more” if not expanded and if the first line is truncated */}
        {!isExpanded && showSeeMore ? (
          <Text onPress={handleSeeMore} style={[styles.seeMoreText, seeMoreStyle]}>
            {' '} {seeMoreText}
          </Text>
        ) : null}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
};

  container: {

pergunta: How to code an api in python to download and chat with a huggingface llm?
resposta:
This is a common and powerful use case. The best way to do this is to use **FastAPI** for the API structure, the **`transformers`** library (and **`torch`**) to load and run the HuggingFace LLM locally, and manage the chat history in memory or via a database.

**⚠️ Important Note on Setup:**
* **Model Size:** LLMs (like Llama 3, Mistral, etc.) are large (GBs). You need sufficient RAM/VRAM to load them.
* **Download Time:** The initial download only happens *once* when the script starts, not on every API request.
* **Hardware:** Using a GPU is highly recommended for reasonable inference speed.

### 🛠️ Prerequisites

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn torch transformers accelerate
```

### 🐍 Python API Code (`main.py`)

This example uses a smaller, optimized model (`microsoft/DialoGPT-medium`) for quick testing. You can replace this with a more powerful model (e.g., `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2`), but be aware of the resource requirements.

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
import time

# --- 1. Model Initialization (Load ONLY ONCE at startup) ---
MODEL_NAME = "microsoft/DialoGPT-medium" # Use a smaller model for testing
# MODEL_NAME = "mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2" # For powerful chat (requires more VRAM)

print(f"Loading model: {MODEL_NAME}...")
try:
    # Determine device (use CUDA if available)
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    print(f"Using device: {device}")
    
    # Load tokenizer and model
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME).to(device)

    # Storage for chat history (required for multi-turn conversation)
    chat_history_ids = None 
    print("Model loaded successfully.")

except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error loading model: {e}")
    # Exit or handle gracefully if model loading fails
    tokenizer = None
    model = None

# --- 2. FastAPI Setup ---
app = FastAPI(title="HuggingFace Chat API")

# Pydantic schema for incoming request
class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str

# --- 3. Inference Function ---
def generate_response(prompt: str):
    """Generates a response using the loaded LLM."""
    global chat_history_ids, model, tokenizer
    
    if model is None or tokenizer is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="LLM not initialized. Check server logs.")

    # Encode the new user input
    new_user_input_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt + tokenizer.eos_token, return_tensors='pt').to(model.device)

    # Append the new input to the previous conversation history
    if chat_history_ids is None:
        bot_input_ids = new_user_input_ids
    else:
        bot_input_ids = torch.cat([chat_history_ids, new_user_input_ids], dim=-1)

    # Generate response (using specific generation parameters)
    chat_history_ids = model.generate(
        bot_input_ids, 
        max_length=1000, 
        pad_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id, 
        do_sample=True, 
        top_k=50, 
        top_p=0.95
    )

    # Decode the response (excluding the input prompt)
    # We decode the full history and then slice off the input length
    response = tokenizer.decode(chat_history_ids[:, bot_input_ids.shape[-1]:][0], skip_special_tokens=True)
    
    return response

# --- 4. API Endpoint ---
@app.post("/chat")
async def chat_endpoint(request: ChatRequest):
    """Accepts a prompt and returns the LLM's response."""
    try:
        start_time = time.time()
        response = generate_response(request.prompt)
        end_time = time.time()

        return {
            "response": response,
            "time_taken_s": round(end_time - start_time, 2)
        }
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Inference error: {e}")
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Internal server error during inference: {e}")

# Optional: Health check
@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    return {"status": "ok", "model_loaded": model is not None}

# --- 5. How to Run ---
# Save the code as main.py and run the following command in your terminal:
# uvicorn main:app --reload
```

### 🚀 How to Run and Test

1. **Run the Server:**
   ```bash
   uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
   ```
2. **Access Docs:** Open your browser to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (FastAPI automatically generates interactive documentation).
3. **Test the Endpoint:** Use the `/chat` POST endpoint with a JSON body:
   ```json
   {
     "prompt": "Hello! I am learning about Python APIs."
   }
   ```
4. **Test Conversation:** Send a follow-up prompt:
   ```json
   {
     "prompt": "What is FastAPI used for?"
   }
   ```
   *(The LLM will remember the context of the previous turn because `chat_history_ids` persists between calls.)*

---

### 💡 Alternative: HuggingFace Inference API (No Local Setup)

If you **do not** have a powerful GPU or limited RAM, you should use the dedicated HuggingFace Inference API. This method is simpler but requires an API token and may incur costs for heavy usage.

**Pros:** Zero local setup, scales easily.
**Cons:** Latency depends on HF servers, requires API key, less control.

```python
import requests
import os

HUGGINGFACE_API_TOKEN = os.getenv("HF_TOKEN")
API_URL = "https://api-inference.huggingface.co/models/mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2"

def query_hf_api(prompt, history=None):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {HUGGINGFACE_API_TOKEN}"}
    payload = {"inputs": prompt}
    
    # Note: Handling multi-turn chat requires formatting the prompt 
    # according to the model's instruction template (e.g., Mistral's chat format).
    
    response = requests.post(API_URL, headers=headers, json=payload)
    
    if response.status_code == 200:
        return response.json()[0]['generated_text']
    else:
        # Handle loading/rate limiting errors
        return f"Error: {response.status_code} - {response.text}"

# This function would then be wrapped in a FastAPI endpoint.
```

### ⚙️ Summary of Approaches

| Feature | Local `transformers` (Recommended) | HuggingFace Inference API |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Setup** | Python, PyTorch, GPU recommended | API Key, Python `requests` |
| **Dependencies** | Heavy (PyTorch, CUDA) | Light |
| **Cost** | Hardware cost | Usage/API token cost |
| **Latency** | Very fast (local) | Variable (network dependent) |
| **Control** | Full control (params, device) | Limited to API settings |
| **Best For** | Production, high volume, dedicated resources | Quick prototypes, low-volume, no local resources |

# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline

# Define a request body model for type checking
class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    message: str

app = FastAPI(title="Hugging Face LLM Chat API")

# Load the model and tokenizer when the server starts
MODEL_NAME = "microsoft/DialoGPT-medium"

try:
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
except Exception as e:
    raise RuntimeError(f"Error downloading the model: {e}")

# Create a text-generation pipeline
chat_generator = pipeline("text-generation", model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer)

@app.post("/chat")
async def chat(chat_req: ChatRequest):
    prompt = chat_req.message.strip()
    
    if not prompt:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="The prompt message is empty.")

    # Generate a response; you can adjust parameters such as max_length and do_sample
    try:
        generated = chat_generator(prompt, max_length=100, num_return_sequences=1)
    except Exception as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Error during generation: {e}")
    
    # Extract the generated text from the output
    response_text = generated[0]["generated_text"]

    return {"response": response_text}

    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
